notes:
The relevant statistics are available at different administrative units:
Planning region There are 5 regions in Singapore. Median size: 136.41 km²
Planning area There are 55 planning areas in Singapore. Planning areas have about 50,000 to 250,000 residents. Median size: 10.60 km²
Subzone There are 332 subzones in Singapore. The average subzone has around 10,000 to 30,000 residents, but the largest has >100,000. Median size: 1.19 km²
The map's population data is grounded on 3 main datasets, all from the 2025 General Household Survey: - **Employed** residents by **planning area** of **residence** _(base employed residence statistic)_. - Resident population by **subzone** of **residence** _(to refine employed residences)_. - **Employed** workers by **planning area of workplace**, broken out by **planning region of residence** _(for workplaces and O/D)_. Links to the tables are in the same order in the Data Source Links section below. --- Population statistics are first extrapolated to final working-population totals (including foreign workforce and excluding invalid resident employment). Employed residence counts are pushed down to the **subzone** level by splitting a planning area's employed residents proportionally to subzones based the subzone's number of residents. Buildings are obtained from Overture Maps and then filtered for demand-relevant buildings. Building types are coarsely classified based on OSM building types (via Overture) and [Singapore's Masterplan zoning](https://eservice.ura.gov.sg/maps/?service=MP), to: residential low/med/high, commercial, office, industrial low/med/high. Floorspace is estimated using a mix of building footprint + height, as well as the plot's max allowed floorspace serving as an upper bound. Residence and workplace statistics are then distributed down to these buildings, weighted by estimated floorspace and a set of manual coefficients. Special workforce demand is first injected before per-building distribution, with their workforce counts subtracted from subzonal totals to prevent double counting. Per-building demand points are then aggregated with a minimum 200 m spacing. Aggregated demand points with less than 50 people are merged into nearby points. Commute flows are assigned using a gravity model constrained by the O/D matrix for (workplace planning area ⟷ residence planning region). Special non-workforce demand is then finally added onto the existing demand data. Non-university/airport points are merged with existing points if necessary. More comprehensive descriptions are available on the [repo's README](https://github.com/Zeepheru/subwaybuilder-singapore-map). — Reviewer refinements (2026-11-14): Source structure: SingStat GHS 2025 combines a register component (population, age, residence geography) with a sample survey of ~27,000 households (labour and place-of-work items). workplace_count re-ruled registered_self_declared — place-of-work counts are expansion-weighted sample estimates, not an enumeration (§4 Expanded sample surveys; CL precedent). Granularity graded by typical unit size, not nominal hierarchy (a city-state has no municipalities): subzone (332; median 1.19 km², ~10–30k residents) ≈ CZ ZSJ-díl by area (1.4–2.4 km² bundle medians) and the doha-zone band by population → ADM4; planning area (55; median ~10 km², 50–250k residents) ≈ CZ obec by area (6.9–7.6 km²) and a Tokyo special ward by population (median 20.5 km², ~350k) → ADM3; planning region (5; median 136 km², ~0.8M residents) → ADM3 by area (Sendai ward 147 km²) / ADM2 by population (kuwait governorates). workplace_granularity re-ruled adm3 — jobs are published by planning area of workplace only. resident_granularity re-ruled adm3 — employed residents are published by planning area only; the subzone layer is register total population used as split weights (flat employment rate within each planning area). Of the literally-true framings, employed_residents@adm3 outscores total_population@adm4 (CL/rio/TW fine-layer reading) and is scored. The as-filed employed_residents@adm4 (0.498, medium) is declined: employment is not measured at subzone grain (cancun-appeal standard). od_metric re-ruled structured_marginals — the 55 × 5 planning area of workplace × planning region of residence table is sampled (§6 enumeration note; CL precedent); the gravity model is constrained to it. od_granularity kept adm3 (destination planning area ADM3; origin region ADM2–3 bounds; adm2 would score 0.426, tier-neutral). Placement kept as filed on both pillars: Overture footprints × manual 8-class weights with URA Master Plan zoning and plot-ratio caps (rio precedent; weights not fit to local totals). Unscored: the non-resident uplift (~871k, MOM pass-type shares) and the Malaysia-commuter subtraction (~150k) are uniform national rescalings that leave the spatial shape unchanged (constant-scaling rule) — no factor moves; institutional workforce points (ministries, hospitals, military) are unscored.
